sentences.text: Counsel for Applicant :- Ritesh Ranjan Chaubey,Pramod Kumar Tiwari,Smt. Usha Tiwari Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Kuldeep Kumar Srivastava Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.

1. Heard Smt. Usha Tiwari, the learned counsel for the applicant and Shri Abhishek Kumar Singh,
learned AGA for the State.
2.
By means of the instant application, the applicant is seeking bail in Case Crime No.515 of 2022 under Sections 406, 420 IPC at police station- Kotwali Nagar District-Faizabad.

3. The aforesaid case has been registered on the basis of an FIR lodged on 03.07.2022 against four persons, including the applicant and his family members, stating that the complainant, who is an advocate by profession, had made some investments on the allurement of the applicant but no returns were paid to him.
By means of the FIR, the complainant has prayed for refund of his amount.
4. In the affidavit filed in support of the application, it has been stated that the applicant is involved Rahul Mishra vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Lko.

entities.text: Rahul Mishra vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Lko
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169104272/
1 in twenty other cases and the learned counsel for the petitioner states that he has been granted bail in four of those cases.
5. Co-accused Shyam Ji Mishra, who is applicant's father has been granted bail by means of order dated 02.11.2023 passed in bail application no. 6577 of 2022.

6. The applicant is languishing in jail since 22.09.2021 and as per the statement of the learned counsel for the applicant, even the charges have not been framed till date.
7.
Learned AGA vehemently opposes the bail prayer of the applicant but he could not dispute the aforesaid aspects of the matter.
8. Having considered the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to released on bail.
9. Accordingly, this bail application stands allowed.
